data.title: The drawing table

memoryNodes.cue: Maya asks because she wants to understand them.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 玛雅真心想理解图画，所以发问。

memoryNodes.cue: Ruth makes a parent feel welcome.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 露丝让家长感到受欢迎。

memoryNodes.cue: Parents stay while children choose what to draw.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 家长留下看护，孩子自己选择画什么。

data.situation:
The studio smelled of paper and new pencils. One child was drawing the centre’s door while another was watching the queue outside. Maya felt genuine interest in their pictures; she asked what the little shapes meant instead of saying every picture was perfect. An amiable volunteer named Ruth pulled out a spare chair for a parent. She spoke so warmly that the parent soon stopped worrying about joining in. Drawing table
Children’s activities require parental supervision.
Ask Ruth for paper and pencils.
Please leave finished pictures on the drying shelf. Parent: Can I stay beside her? I do not want to interfere.
Ruth: Of course. Let her choose the colours, and ask if she wants help.
Maya: I appreciate you making space for us.
Ruth: There is room for one more chair.
By the window, an older visitor showed a sketch of the canal. His picture seemed to inspire a child to begin a drawing of her own.

readingBlocks.en: The studio smelled of paper and new pencils. One child was drawing the centre’s door while another was watching the queue outside. Maya felt genuine interest in their pictures; she asked what the little shapes meant instead of saying every picture was perfect. An amiable volunteer named Ruth pulled out a spare chair for a parent. She spoke so warmly that the parent soon stopped worrying about joining in.
readingBlocks.zh: 画室里有纸和新铅笔的气味。一个孩子在画中心的门，另一个望着外面的队伍。玛雅真心对他们的画感兴趣；她问那些小形状表示什么，而没有说每张画都完美。一位叫露丝的友善志愿者为一位家长拉出备用椅子。她说话很温和，家长很快不再担心自己能否参与。

readingBlocks.title: On the materials box

readingBlocks.en:
Parent: Can I stay beside her? I do not want to interfere.
Ruth: Of course. Let her choose the colours, and ask if she wants help.
Maya: I appreciate you making space for us.
Ruth: There is room for one more chair.
By the window, an older visitor showed a sketch of the canal. His picture seemed to inspire a child to begin a drawing of her own.
readingBlocks.zh:
家长：我能坐在她旁边吗？我不想过多干涉。
露丝：当然。让她自己选颜色，需要时再问她要不要帮助。
玛雅：谢谢你为我们腾地方。
露丝：还能再放一把椅子。
窗边，一位年长访客展示运河速写。他的画似乎启发一个孩子开始画自己的作品。

glossary.note: 本例为感情真诚；不是物品真伪。
glossary.example: Maya shows genuine interest in the pictures.
glossary.exampleZh: 玛雅真心对这些图画感兴趣。

externalEvidence.definition: not pretended; sincerely felt or expressed

glossary.note: 常形容人的性情与态度；与amicable关系和睦区分。
glossary.example: Ruth is an amiable volunteer who welcomes everyone.
glossary.exampleZh: 露丝是一位欢迎每个人的友善志愿者。

glossary.note: parental supervision；常与require或under连用，表示家长在场看护或监督。
glossary.example: The children’s activities require parental supervision.
glossary.exampleZh: 儿童活动需要家长看护。

externalEvidence.label: Cambridge Dictionary
externalEvidence.reviewFinding: Cambridge collocation URL in source review supports parental supervision; original parent supervision preserved.

glossary.note: interfere in/with；此处是干涉他人的选择。
glossary.example: The parent wants to help without interfering.
glossary.exampleZh: 家长想帮忙，但不想过多干涉。

externalEvidence.label: Oxford Learner’s Dictionaries
externalEvidence.reviewFinding: Intrusion into another person’s affairs; local intervention/obstruction candidates do not specify this use.

glossary.note: appreciate something/someone doing something；不接to do。
glossary.example: I appreciate you making space for us.

externalEvidence.definition: recognize with gratitude; be grateful for

glossary.note: inspire someone to do something；不是呼吸义。
glossary.example: The sketch inspired a child to start drawing.
glossary.exampleZh: 速写启发一个孩子开始画画。

externalEvidence.definition: serve as the inciting cause of
